stem: Explain the difference between an array and a record. [3]

points.description: An array holds items that all have the same data type, a record can hold items of different types
Array elements are accessed by an index (position)
Record fields are accessed by their names

stem: A school stores for each learner the learner's name, form, mean mark and whether the learner has paid fees. Write the pseudocode to define a record type `TLearner`. [4]

points.description: TYPE TLearner ... ENDTYPE structure
Name declared as STRING
Form declared as INTEGER and mean mark declared as REAL
Paid declared as BOOLEAN, each with the DECLARE keyword

answerSpec.markingNotes:
Example answer: ```
TYPE TLearner
    DECLARE Name : STRING
    DECLARE Form : INTEGER
    DECLARE MeanMark : REAL
    DECLARE FeesPaid : BOOLEAN
ENDTYPE
```

explanation: One DECLARE line per field.
hints: Start with TYPE and end with ENDTYPE.

stem: Explain two benefits of storing learner details in an array of records instead of a separate array for each detail. [3]

points.description: All details of one learner are stored together, so they stay linked (for example when sorting)
The program is easier to read because a field is named, such as Learner[1].Name
A whole record can be passed to a subroutine or written to a file as one item

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The details of one learner stay together, so they cannot get out of step when the data is processed. The code is easier to read because fields are named, and a whole record can be passed to a subroutine as one item.

explanation: Grouping and readability.
hints: Think about what is repeated when the data is in separate arrays.

stem:
A clinic stores its appointments in an array `Appointment` of five records of type `TAppointment`, with the fields `PatientName`, `Phone` and `Attended`. The data is:

| Index | PatientName | Phone | Attended |
|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| 1 | Sipho Dube | 0772000111 | TRUE |
| 2 | Thandeka Moyo | 0712333444 | FALSE |
| 3 | Nyasha Chari | 0782555666 | TRUE |
| 4 | Tatenda Banda | 0733777888 | TRUE |
| 5 | Rudo Zulu | 0774999000 | FALSE |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which data type is most suitable for `Phone`?

options.rationale: The leading zero would be lost.
A telephone number has no fractional part.
Correct.
A Boolean holds only TRUE or FALSE.

parts.explanation: A telephone number is an identifier, not used in arithmetic.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Give two reasons for your answer to part (a).

points.description: Telephone numbers begin with 0, which would be lost if stored as a number
They are not used in calculations such as addition

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A telephone number begins with 0, which would be lost in a number type, and it is never used in calculations.

parts.label: (c)
parts.workedSolution: Attended is TRUE for Sipho Dube, Nyasha Chari and Tatenda Banda.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Write pseudocode that counts the patients who attended and outputs the count.

points.description: A loop from 1 to 5 with the counter set to 0 before it
Tests Appointment[Index].Attended and adds 1 to the counter, then outputs the counter after the loop

answerSpec.markingNotes:
Example answer: ```
Count ← 0
FOR Index ← 1 TO 5
    IF Appointment[Index].Attended = TRUE THEN
        Count ← Count + 1
    ENDIF
NEXT Index
OUTPUT Count
```

parts.explanation: Count with a loop and a field test.

explanation: Counting records in an array of appointments.
hints: Count the rows in which Attended is TRUE.
Use a loop with a counter and an IF.
